title: assess signals document
description: Output of skills/assess/scripts/assess_signals.py: a run stamp plus one block per scan. Generated from lib/run_context_types.py by lib/signals_schema.py.

reason.description: Why the block is unavailable, usually 'code: sentence'; only blocks with a named entry list their codes. A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

agent_consistency.description: Cross-agent instruction consistency (lib/agent_consistency.py): the root instruction files of every agent system present at HEAD (Claude Code, AGENTS.md, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Aider, Junie, Amazon Q, Kiro, Continue, Zed), the check commands and thresholds they disagree on, and how each links to one canonical file.

reason.description: Why the block is unavailable.

systems_total.description: Agent systems with a root instruction file.

applicable.description: False with fewer than two systems: nothing to agree with.

canonical.description: The canonical file: AGENTS.md when present, else the first root file in system order; null with no instruction file.

files.description: Each root-context instruction file, its system and how it links to the canonical.

value.description: The command, or the threshold keyword; dropped from counts-only output.

divergences.description: A command one system names and another does not, or a threshold two state differently.

conflicts.description: The agent-consistency row's level 1 signal: divergences; null when not applicable.

unlinked.description: The level 2 signal: systems not linked to the canonical file; null when not applicable.

consistent.description: No divergence and every system linked; null when not applicable.

pointer.description: The exact pointer line for the tool; dropped from counts-only output.

symlink.description: A symlink command; null for Aider (config-only).

not_read.description: A list of strings; counts-only output keeps only its length.

reason.description: 'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: shallow_clone (the checkout is a shallow clone, so a reverting or rewriting commit may be cut from the history read); shallow_unknown (git could not confirm the checkout is a full clone); not_a_repo (the path is not a git repository, or one with no commits); no_git (git is not installed where the scan ran); git_failed (a git read past the windowed log (a patch-id, numstat or blame read) failed on a repository the log could read); git_timeout (a git read took longer than the scan allows). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

agent_outcome.description: Revert and rework rate of the agent commits of the run window (lib/agent_outcome.py, issue #1085). Informational: no Step, count or headline reads it. The agent commits are those ai_usage counts in agent_either_commits (an AI-assistant trailer or an agent author). Reverted: a later commit's 'This reverts commit' message names it, or a later commit's diff is its exact inverse (equal git patch-id). Reworked: git blame, rework_days after the commit, no longer attributes some line it added to it. A share with nothing to divide by is null with a token reason.

window.description: The history window read, as in ai_usage.

since.description: The window as an absolute git --since bound; dropped in counts-only output.

informational.description: Always true: nothing scores this block.

agent_rule.description: Which commits count as agent commits (trailer_or_author).

reverted_commits.description: Agent commits later reverted, by message or by inverse diff.

reverted_by_message.description: Agent commits a 'This reverts commit' message names.

reverted_by_restore.description: Agent commits a later commit's inverse diff undoes; a git revert usually counts here too.

revert_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of agent commits later reverted; null when nothing was counted.

rework_days.description: The rework span, in days after each agent commit.

rework_observed_commits.description: Agent commits at least rework_days older than HEAD.

rework_sampled_commits.description: Of those, the newest checked (at most 50).

reworked_commits.description: Sampled agent commits with an added line rewritten or removed within rework_days.

rework_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of sampled agent commits reworked within rework_days; null when nothing was counted.

rework_null_reason.description: Why rework_share is null: no_agent_commits or none_old_enough.

limits.description: A list of strings; counts-only output keeps only its length.

reason.description: Why the block is unavailable. A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

ai_usage.description: Agent involvement in the commits of the run window (lib/ai_usage.py), counted from git history. An agent identity is matched by trailer (Co-Authored-By and similar) or by author against the accounts confirmed in [identities], the pinned agent rules and any [[ai_usage.agent_identities]] rules of --fleet-config. Counts are commits; shares are of total_commits. A lower bound: an agent that leaves no trace is not counted.

window.description: The history window read, for example 6mo.

since.description: The window as an absolute git --since bound (@<epoch>, counted back from HEAD's commit time); dropped in counts-only output.

merge_rule.description: How merge commits are treated (excluded: not counted).

agent_trailer_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of commits carrying an agent trailer; null when nothing was counted.

agent_authored_commits.description: Commits whose author an agent identity matches.

agent_authored_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of commits whose author an agent identity matches; null when nothing was counted.

agent_either_commits.description: Commits with an agent trailer or an agent author.

agent_either_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of commits with an agent trailer or an agent author; null when nothing was counted.

dependency_bot_commits.description: Commits by a dependency-update bot (Dependabot, Renovate); never counted as agent work.

token_user_commits.description: Commits by a GitLab access-token user (project_<id>_bot_<hex>) not promoted to agent; a config rule or token_users_as_agents promotes one.

agent_identity_rule_commits.description: Commits each [[ai_usage.agent_identities]] rule matched, a positional list in rule order; the rule patterns themselves are never written.

identities_awaiting_confirmation.description: Accounts in the window that look automated (a [bot] suffix, a GitLab token user, a bot or AI tool name) and are neither classified in the [identities] config section nor counted by an agent rule (#765). A next step for the human, never a score; the accounts are listed only by scripts/identity_candidates.py.

covered_agents.description: A list of strings; counts-only output keeps only its length.

covered_author_agents.description: A list of strings; counts-only output keeps only its length.

limits.description: A list of strings; counts-only output keeps only its length.

ci_checks.description: Does CI run a test or lint check (lib/ci_checks.py), read from the git-tracked CI files and the GitLab includes resolved offline (lib/ci_includes.py: local files, and project or component files of clones in the --ghsync-root). test_or_lint_configured is true when an own or included CI line runs one, false when none does and every include resolved, and null (unknown) when a CI file pulls jobs from a file this run could not read (an unresolved GitLab include, a reusable workflow in another repository); basis says which. Under --platform, a repository with an unresolved GitLab include also gets GitLab's merged configuration from the CI lint API (lib/hosting/gitlab_ci_lint.py), counted apart in merged_check_commands; a template resolved offline wins. enforced_check_runs (issue #775) is the same test with masked checks left out (|| true, continue-on-error: true, allow_failure: true, set +e without a re-raise; lib/ci_masking.py) and checks off the ordinary triggers left out (lib/ci_triggers.py); masked_check_commands and off_trigger_check_commands count the lines left out. lint_runs (issue #782) is the enforced test for lint lines only (Layer 3 level 1); a check target or script that may run a linter inside it reads null. CI files of other systems are not parsed (issues #787, #928): unread_ci_files counts them, and with no readable check one makes basis unread_ci_system and enforced_check_runs null (and lint_runs null with no readable lint line). The unread-CI paths, all relative to the repository root: Jenkinsfile, .circleci/config.yml, bitbucket-pipelines.yml, .travis.yml, azure-pipelines.yml, azure-pipelines.yaml, .azure-pipelines.yml, .azure-pipelines.yaml, .buildkite/pipeline.yml, .buildkite/pipeline.yaml, buildkite.yml, buildkite.yaml, .ci.yaml (Flutter Cocoon / LUCI), .prow.yaml, .zuul.yaml, .drone.yml, .woodpecker.yml, .cirrus.yml, appveyor.yml, .semaphore/semaphore.yml, cloudbuild.yaml, bitrise.yml and codemagic.yaml; any *.star or *.cfg file under infra/config/ (LUCI project configuration); any *.yml or *.yaml file under .azure/pipelines/, eng/pipelines/, .azure-pipelines/, azure-pipelines/ (Azure Pipelines) or .woodpecker/; and any file under zuul.d/ (lib/unread_ci.py). Off-repository CI (issue #928): under --platform, when more than half of the sampled merged pull requests carry a check run or commit status of a known external CI system (lib/external_ci.py, at most two GET calls per sampled pull request), the false cases read null with basis external_ci; offline, a root Prow OWNERS_ALIASES file with no CI file of any kind reads null with basis external_ci_marker. Neither earns credit.

reason.description: Why the block is unavailable.

check_commands.description: CI lines that run a test or lint check.

included_files.description: CI files that pull jobs from elsewhere.

included_check_commands.description: Lines of resolved included files that run a test or lint check.

resolved_includes.description: Include items whose every file was read.

unresolved_includes.description: Include items not read (status other than resolved).

kind.description: local, project, component, template, remote, or unknown (an include entry this reader cannot parse; status unparsed).

id.description: gitlab_project:<path> or gitlab_component:<path>; null for the other kinds.

status.description: resolved; toolkit_gate (the toolkit's own regression gate template, known to run no project tests); or why not: no_root, not_cloned, file_missing, not_offline (template, remote), glob, bad_path, depth_limit, file_limit, unparsed, ref_missing (a pin the clone does not hold).

ref_basis.description: How the file was read: at the pinned ref, at the clone's HEAD (no pin), or from the work tree; null when not resolved.

depth.description: Include level: 1 for the repository's own include.

includes.description: One record per include item, nested includes after their parent; no file name or text.

merged_config.description: The CI lint API read: not_read (offline), not_needed (every include resolved offline), read, invalid (GitLab marked the configuration invalid) or unavailable.

merged_config_reason.description: The reason code when merged_config is unavailable (no_access, not_found, not_gitlab, ...); null otherwise.

merged_check_commands.description: Lines of the merged configuration that run a test or lint check; the text is never published.

test_or_lint_configured.description: The CI test-or-lint signal: true, false, or null when included jobs may hold the check or a Maven run skips its tests.

basis.description: The reason for test_or_lint_configured: check_command or merged_config (true; the second when only the merged configuration ran a check), included_jobs or merged_config_partial (null; the second when the merged configuration was read with no check but may lack jobs: an include under rules:, or a trigger: child pipeline), check_target (null: no check, but a Maven or Gradle run with its tests skipped, mvn -DskipTests verify or ./gradlew check -x test, which may still run a lint task), unread_ci_system (false: no readable check, but a CI file of a system the scan does not parse is tracked), external_ci or external_ci_marker (false: no readable check, but CI runs off the repository; as enforced_basis), no_check_command or no_ci (false).

enforced_check_runs.description: Layer 5 level 1: true when a CI line runs a check that can fail its job on ordinary changes, null when none does but included jobs, unsettled triggers, a committed script the tree does not hold, a target whose recipe is not read, a CI system the scan does not parse or an external CI system may hold one, else false.

enforced_basis.description: The reason for enforced_check_runs: enforced_check (true), included_jobs, unknown_trigger, check_may_pass (a check whose failure the step may hide: pytest || echo failed, an if or while condition, an until loop that breaks out, a check before && with more of the step after it, a { } group or function called in such a position; issue #1008), script_not_found, check_target or unread_ci_system (null), external_ci (null: an external check context on merged changes under --platform; more than half of the sampled merged pull requests carry a check run or commit status of a known external CI system such as Buildkite, LUCI, Prow tide or Azure Pipelines, read with at most two GET calls per sampled pull request; it never gives credit), external_ci_marker (null: offline, a root Prow OWNERS_ALIASES file with no CI file present, neither a workflow, a .gitlab-ci.yml nor an unread CI file; an OWNERS file alone is not a marker), not_enforced, no_check_command or no_ci (false).

masked_check_commands.description: CI lines that run a check whose failure cannot fail the job.

off_trigger_check_commands.description: Unmasked CI check lines whose workflow or job does not run on ordinary changes (workflow_dispatch or schedule only, a manual GitLab job).

lint_runs.description: Layer 3 level 1 (issue #782): true when a CI line runs a linter that can fail its job on ordinary changes (not --version or --help), or a step uses a known lint action (golangci-lint-action, ruff-action, super-linter, reviewdog), null when none does but included jobs, unsettled triggers, a lint script the tree does not hold or a check target or script that may lint inside it could hold one, or when the only static gate is a compiler run with warnings as errors or a .NET build's analysers (issue #926), else false. A formatter that rewrites files counts only when a later line of its job runs git diff --exit-code.

lint_basis.description: The reason for lint_runs: lint_command (true), included_jobs, merged_config_partial, unknown_trigger, check_may_pass, script_not_found, check_target, unread_ci_system, external_ci or external_ci_marker (null; as enforced_basis), analysers_in_build (null: a CI .NET build runs the analysers a committed Directory.Build.props or .csproj turns on with EnforceCodeStyleInBuild or AnalysisLevel; their severities live in .editorconfig, which the scan does not evaluate), compiler_gate_only (null: the only static gate is a compiler run with warnings as errors, such as mix compile --warnings-as-errors, -Werror or TreatWarningsAsErrors; issue #926), not_enforced, no_lint_command or no_ci (false).

unread_ci_files.description: Tracked CI files of systems the scan does not parse, at the unread-CI paths the block description lists; a count, never the paths.

reason.description: Why the block is unavailable. A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

coverage_gate.description: Committed line-coverage thresholds (lib/testing/coverage_gate.py), read from config and CI files at HEAD, never from measured coverage. Each gate keeps its threshold as written beside threshold_percent, the same value as a percentage (a JaCoCo ratio 0.80 is 80).

reason.description: Why the block is unavailable.

configured.description: True when any gate gates something (a non-zero threshold, or a null one from a tool default or a templated flag). Read from configuration text at HEAD; was enforced before issue #783. A root coverage.py gate listed on a scoped run whose hold on the scope is not resolved (unmeasured_reason root_coverage_config_unresolved, issue #1032) is not counted here.

threshold.description: The threshold as written; null when not read (a template variable, a tool default).

threshold_percent.description: The threshold as a percentage: as written for percent, times 100 for ratio; null for uncovered_count, missed_ratio (a JaCoCo MISSEDRATIO maximum) or a threshold not read.

gates.description: Each gate found, with its file and 1-based line.

max_threshold_percent.description: The highest non-null threshold_percent across the gates; null when no gate has one. An unresolved root gate on a scoped run (issue #1032) and a Codecov patch target (issue #882) are left out.

threshold_meets_minimum.description: The Layer 6 level 1 signal: true when a counted gate's threshold_percent is at least 50; null (unknown) when none is but a counted gate's percentage was not read, or when a repository holding a go.mod or Cargo.toml has no gate of that language and none of at least 50 for another, or when a Codecov project status target is auto or missing, or the only Codecov status is a patch status, and no other gate decides it (issue #882), or when a scoped run cannot tell whether the root coverage.py floor governs the scope and that floor would change the reading (see unmeasured_reason); false otherwise. Gates counted are those enforced counts.

unmeasured_reason.description: Why threshold_meets_minimum is null when no gate of the repository's Go or Rust module is found: go_rust_gate_form_not_read when the repository holds a go.mod or Cargo.toml with no gate read for it and none of at least 50 percent for another language (issue #937), so its gate may be a script this scan does not read; root_coverage_config_unresolved on a scoped run when the repository root's coverage.py floor would change the reading but where CI runs coverage is not resolved (issue #1032); codecov_target_not_read when the only gate that could reach 50 percent is a Codecov project status with an auto, missing or non-numeric target, codecov_patch_only when it is a Codecov patch status, which bounds changed lines only (issue #882); null otherwise.

enforced_meets_minimum.description: The Layer 6 level 1 signal (issue #921): threshold_meets_minimum with a CI run required. True when it is true and an enforced CI line (unmasked, on ordinary triggers; lib/ci_masking.py, lib/ci_triggers.py) passes a counted threshold of at least 50 itself or runs the tool that reads it; null when threshold_meets_minimum is null or the run cannot be told (see enforced_basis); false otherwise.

enforced_basis.description: The reason for enforced_meets_minimum: ci_run (true); no_gate, threshold_below_minimum, not_run_in_ci and no_ci (false); threshold_not_read, unknown_trigger, check_may_pass (the run's failure may not fail its job: pytest --cov || echo failed; issue #1008), indirect_run (a check target or script such as make test may run it), included_jobs, unread_ci_system and status_check_unconfirmed (a Codecov status target, which no CI line runs and which gates a merge only when branch protection requires it; issue #882) (null).

not_detected.description: A list of strings; counts-only output keeps only its length.

delivery.description: How work flows through review to merge (lib/hosting/delivery.py), from one shared sample of up to 30 changes merged inside the run window, newest merge first (the sample review_reality reads). A platform block: present only under --platform (absent otherwise); a refused read is available false with a reason (no_access on HTTP 403), never zeros. Durations are hours; shares are of merged_count.

sample_page_size.description: Changes per heavy read of the sample (lib/hosting/merged_sample.py PAGE_SIZE, or half of it after one retry on HTTP 502 or 504); null when no heavy read was made.

unconfirmed_ai_accounts.description: Distinct sampled accounts that are name-only AI matches awaiting confirmation in [identities] (#883): change authors, and on GitLab note authors. A non-zero count is why the share it would decide reads null.

reviewed_share.description: Share (0 to 1) of changes with a review by an account other than the author (on GitLab also an approval, a human comment or AI review); null also when a GitLab merge request's notes decide nothing; null when nothing was counted.

bot_sequence.description: One token per sampled change, in the order of sequence: bot, none or unknown (review-bot output, #943).

layer_grades.description: Deterministic layer grades (lib/layer_grades.py): the best instruction-file grade and where the agent instruction files are. Tokens and a boolean, kept whole by counts-only output; no path is carried.

instruction_presence.description: root: a file at a root location (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .github/copilot-instructions.md and the others instruction_files grades) or one the tool loads at session start, always loaded. nested_only: no root file, but a nested or path-scoped file (pkg/AGENTS.md, a .claude/rules file with paths), loaded on demand where the agent works. none: no instruction file at any known location. Null when there is no root file and the nested_instructions scan did not run.

instruction_file_present.description: True for root and nested_only, false for none, null with instruction_presence. Layer 0 level 1 of the default maturity model reads it.

instructions_grade.description: Best letter grade (A to F) of the files instruction_presence counts: the root files, else the always-loaded or nested ones. Null only for none.

reason.description: 'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: knowledge_base (the repository is a knowledge base (archetype knowledge-base), which takes no code patches); org_policy_not_read (the repository holds no security policy, and the owner's shared .github repository, whose policy GitHub shows on it, was not read (offline, no --platform, a remote not on github.com, or gh not signed in)). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_remote (the repository has no github.com remote, so there is no owner .github repository to read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: network (no AI review step is committed in CI, and a headless run without --platform makes no GitHub or GitLab read); no_remote (no AI review step is committed in CI and the repository has no GitHub or GitLab remote, so there are no merged changes to read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: secret_scanning_not_read (no secrets scan runs in CI, and the repository is on GitHub, whose own secret scanning and push protection were not read); ci_includes_unresolved (no secrets scan was found in the CI read, and a GitLab include that could hold one (a local, project or remote file) was not read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_grimp (grimp, the Python import-graph builder, is not installed); no_networkx (networkx, which the structure metrics need, is not installed); grimp_failed (grimp could not build the Python import graph); no_python_packages (a Python repository with no importable package); no_import_graph_<language> (no import graph builder exists yet for the dominant source language, for example no_import_graph_rust); invalid_import_graph (a builder returned a graph that breaks the module-graph contract); no_source_files (the scope holds no source file in a language the assess skill recognises). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.

'code: sentence'. The codes name the missing piece: no_ownership_map (the repository commits no ownership or boundary map (CODEOWNERS, an ARCHITECTURE module list) for the drift check to read). A counts-only document keeps only the leading code, or unavailable when the reason has no code.
